headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risk: Chatwoot can ingest customer text while PaddleOCR can parse documents/images, creating a default path for untrusted content to flow into downstream actions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Chatwoot ingests customer messages and reports, while PaddleOCR processes documents/images and can run browsers. If Chatwoot content is fed into PaddleOCR or vice versa through a shared workspace or manual handoff, untrusted text can be treated as instructions. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is inferred and kept at medium.
conditions: IF Chatwoot outputs are copied into PaddleOCR prompts or OCR pipelines without sanitization
IF both agents are connected through a shared filesystem or message queue
mitigations: Add a strict delimiter and instruction/data separator in handoffs
Disable automatic execution of any text extracted from documents
Review one sample transfer for prompt-like content before enabling automation
Use a read-only staging folder for exchanged files
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all cross-agent content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, orders, and messages; PaddleOCR touches documents and images. If customer artifacts are routed through PaddleOCR, sensitive data can be exposed in OCR logs or outputs. The profiles do not show shared storage or direct upload behavior, so the risk is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF customer records or support attachments are sent to PaddleOCR for OCR
IF OCR outputs are stored in a shared workspace accessible to Chatwoot
mitigations: Restrict OCR input to redacted samples only
Turn off retention for temporary OCR artifacts
Separate support and OCR workspaces
Check one OCR job for sensitive-field leakage
requires-engineering: enforce field-level redaction before OCR

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Chatwoot has broad network egress and PaddleOCR has allowlisted egress plus browser execution, but neither profile shows filesystem write, git, or shared mutable-resource access. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely; only limited overlap through networked APIs is visible.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same external API or database
IF an orchestrator maps both to the same mutable workspace
mitigations: Keep each agent on separate credentials
Avoid shared writable directories
Audit API destinations before enabling both
Use per-agent job queues
requires-engineering: add locking for any shared mutable resource

D_cascading_error.rationale: Chatwoot produces customer-facing support content and PaddleOCR converts documents/images into extracted text. If PaddleOCR output is treated as authoritative by Chatwoot workflows, OCR mistakes can cascade into incorrect replies or actions. No verification step is documented, so the interaction is inferred from the profiles.
conditions: IF PaddleOCR output is inserted into Chatwoot replies or macros without human review
IF Chatwoot automations act on OCR-extracted fields
mitigations: Require human review before sending any OCR-derived reply
Sample-check extracted fields against source images
Limit automation to low-risk templates
Mark OCR confidence in downstream records
requires-engineering: add validation rules for extracted entities

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data and messages, while PaddleOCR processes documents and images. The profiles do not specify residency, certifications, or retention differences, so no concrete compliance breach is established. The main concern is a possible mismatch if regulated customer documents are OCRed and then retained or transmitted differently.
conditions: IF regulated customer documents are processed by PaddleOCR
IF Chatwoot and PaddleOCR retain the same data class under different policies
mitigations: Confirm retention settings for both systems
Avoid sending regulated documents to OCR unless necessary
Document the data flow for support attachments
Delete temporary OCR artifacts after use
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls
